explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM evaluation against human evaluation using multiple meta-evaluation benchmarks (SummEval, Topical-Chat, QAGS) with correlation analysis on shared criteria

prompts.notes: Full prompts with task introduction, evaluation criteria, and evaluation steps are provided verbatim in the main text, including specific examples for summarization (coherence) and dialogue (engagingness)

guidelines.notes: Human evaluation guidelines are referenced from original benchmark papers (SummEval, Topical-Chat, QAGS) but not reproduced in detail; evaluation criteria and scale definitions are provided

sample_size.validated_by_both: standard benchmark sizes (SummEval, Topical-Chat, QAGS datasets)
sample_size.notes: Uses established meta-evaluation benchmarks with human ratings; exact sample sizes not specified in provided text

quantitative_scores.notes: Average across all criteria on SummEval

validation_results.summary_finding: G-EVAL with GPT-4 achieves Spearman correlations of 0.514 (overall) with human judgments on summarization, outperforming all previous methods. However, LLM evaluators show bias towards LLM-generated texts even when human judges prefer human-written summaries.

criteria_mapping.notes: SummEval uses coherence, consistency, fluency, relevance; Topical-Chat uses naturalness, coherence, engagingness, groundedness; LLM evaluates consistency on QAGS benchmark
